turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: Two days ago while playing football, my right ring finger got caught in another player’s jersey and they pulled away hard. Since then I’ve had progressive swelling and pain around the distal joint, and I can’t flex it at that joint when I make a fist.

I’m sorry that happened. **Question 1:** When you look at the finger, do you see any **deformity** or a **visible “droop”/loss of the fingertip’s normal position** (especially at the distal joint), compared with the other fingers?

Patient: Yes—my right ring finger looks a bit drooped with the fingertip held more extended at the distal joint compared to my other fingers. I also notice the swelling there, and it feels painful when I try to bend it.
**Question 2:** Did you notice an **audible pop** or sudden sharp pain at the moment it was pulled, and did the pain start immediately?

Doctor: Did you notice an audible pop or sudden sharp pain at the moment it was pulled, and did the pain start immediately? Patient: I didn’t hear a pop, but I had a sudden sharp pain right when it was pulled away, and the pain started right away.

**Question 3:** Is the finger **tender specifically on the palm side (volar aspect)** near the **base of the distal joint** (where the tendon would be), or is tenderness more on the back side (dorsal)?
Patient: The tenderness feels mostly on the palm side near the base of that distal joint, and it’s very sore when I press there. It feels less tender on the back side.
**Question 4:** Can you fully **straighten** the distal joint, or is it also limited—i.e., is the main problem that you **can’t flex** the distal joint (DIP) while extension is relatively preserved?

Patient: I can straighten the distal joint fairly well, but when I try to make a fist I can’t bend/flex at the DIP—it stays held more extended and it really hurts. Extension seems less limited than the flexing.
**Question 5:** Do you have any **numbness/tingling** in that fingertip, or is sensation and color/temperature of the fingertip normal?
Patient: No, I don’t have numbness or tingling, and the fingertip feels normal in sensation and color/temperature. It’s mainly swelling, pain, and the trouble flexing the distal joint.
**Question 6:** Is there any **open wound** or bruising/skin break over the distal joint, or is it closed injury only?
Patient: It’s a closed injury—no open wound or skin break that I can see, just swelling and soreness around the distal joint, with no bruising I’d call significant.
**Question 7:** Have you noticed whether the **ring finger nail/fingertip** looks normal, and is there any **inability to fully extend the DIP** as well (or is extension mostly okay)?

Patient: My fingertip and nail look normal—no deformity of the nail. I can fully straighten/extend the DIP pretty well; the main issue is I can’t flex it when I make a fist and it stays more extended.

**Question 8:** When you press along the **volar side at the base of the distal phalanx** (where the flexor tendon inserts), is there a **focal “gap” or point of maximal tenderness** suggesting a tendon injury?

Patient: Yes, there’s a very focal spot of maximal tenderness on the volar side at the base of the distal phalanx, and pressing right there really hurts. I don’t feel any obvious skin break—just that pinpoint tenderness.
**Question 9:** Does the finger show a **“mallet” pattern** (DIP droops at rest and you can’t actively extend), or is it more the opposite—**DIP held extended and you can’t actively flex**?

Patient: It’s the opposite of a mallet pattern—the distal joint is held more extended at rest, and I can’t actively flex the DIP when I try to make a fist. Extension is relatively preserved compared with flexion, and it mainly hurts around that volar base of the distal joint.

**Question 10:** Is the injury specifically at the **flexor side of the DIP** consistent with a **jersey pull**, and do you have any difficulty flexing the **middle phalanx** or is it isolated to the **DIP flexion**?

“Yes, the main issue is flexion at the distal joint—the DIP can’t flex when I make a fist. My middle phalanx flexion seems pretty normal, and the problem feels isolated to that DIP on the volar side where it’s most tender.”
**Question 11:** Any history of **bleeding disorders** or are you on **blood thinners** (or do you bruise easily), given the tendon/soft-tissue injury?
Patient: No, I don’t have any bleeding disorders, I’m not on blood thinners, and I don’t bruise easily.
**Question 12:** Do you have any **fever**, spreading redness, or warmth over the finger/hand (suggesting infection), or is it purely traumatic swelling/pain?
Patient: No fever, and there’s no spreading redness or significant warmth—it's just traumatic swelling and pain around the distal joint.
